arxiv-1508-04181.title: Distinguishability times and asymmetry monotone-based quantum speed limits in the Bloch ball
arxiv-1508-04181.creator: T.J. Volkoff, K.B. Whaley
arxiv-1508-04181.description: Abstract For both unitary and open qubit dynamics, we compare asymmetry monotone-based bounds on the minimal time required for an initial qubit state to evolve to a final qubit state from which it is probabilistically distinguishable with fixed minimal error probability (i.e., the minimal error distinguishability time).

arxiv-1910-14604.title: A Lyapunov-like Characterization of Predefined-Time Stability
arxiv-1910-14604.creator: Esteban Jiménez-Rodríguez, Aldo Jonathan Muñoz-Vázquez, Juan Diego Sánchez-Torres, Michael Defoort and Alexander G. Loukianov
arxiv-1910-14604.description: Abstract This technical note studies Lyapunov-like conditions to ensure a class of dynamical systems to exhibit predefined-time stability. The origin of a dynamical system is predefined-time stable if it is fixed-time stable and an upper bound of the settling-time function can be arbitrarily chosen a priori through a suitable selection of the system parameters.

arxiv-2011-07425.title: Van Vleck excitons in Ca 2 RuO 4
arxiv-2011-07425.creator: P. M. Sarte, C. Stock, B. R. Ortiz, K. H. Hong, S. D. Wilson
arxiv-2011-07425.description: Abstract A framework is presented for modeling and understanding magnetic excitations in localized, intermediate coupling magnets where the interplay between spin-orbit coupling, magnetic exchange, and crystal field effects are known to create a complex landscape of unconventional magnetic behaviors and ground states.

arxiv-2107-03506.title: Communication networks and group effectiveness: the case of English Wikipedia
arxiv-2107-03506.creator: Agnieszka Rychwalska, Szymon Talaga, Karolina Ziembowicz, Dariusz Jemielniak
arxiv-2107-03506.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Agnieszka Rychwalska, Szymon Talaga, Karolina Ziembowicz, Dariusz Jemielniak. A selection of intellectual goods produced by online communities – e.g. open source software or knowledge bases like Wikipedia – are in daily use by a broad audience, and thus their quality impacts the public at large. Yet, it is still unclear what contributes to the effectiveness of such online peer production systems: what conditions or social processes help them deliver quality products. Specifically, while co-contribution (i.e.

arxiv-2205-15683.title: Why are NLP Models Fumbling at Elementary Math? A Survey of Deep Learning based Word Problem Solvers Work done while author was here
arxiv-2205-15683.creator: Sowmya S Sundaram, Sairam Gurajada, Marco Fisichella, Deepak P, Savitha Sam Abraham
arxiv-2205-15683.description: Abstract From the latter half of the last decade, there has been a growing interest in developing algorithms for automatically solving mathematical word problems (MWP). It is a challenging and unique task that demands blending surface level text pattern recognition with mathematical reasoning.

arxiv-2207-08867.title: MCTensor: A High-Precision Deep Learning Library with Multi-Component Floating-Point
arxiv-2207-08867.creator: Tao Yu, Wentao Guo, Jianan Canal Li, Tiancheng Yuan, Christopher De Sa
arxiv-2207-08867.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce MCTensor, a library based on PyTorch for providing general-purpose and high-precision arithmetic for DL training. MCTensor is used in the same way as PyTorch Tensor: we implement multiple basic, matrix-level computation operators and NN modules for MCTensor with identical PyTorch interface.

arxiv-2210-11348.title: Hypernetworks in Meta-Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2210-11348.creator: Jacob Beck, Matthew Jackson, Risto Vuorio, Shimon Whiteson
arxiv-2210-11348.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jacob Beck, Matthew Jackson, Risto Vuorio, Shimon Whiteson. Training a reinforcement learning (RL) agent on a real-world robotics task remains generally impractical due to sample inefficiency. Multi-task RL and meta-RL aim to improve sample efficiency by generalizing over a distribution of related tasks. However, doing so is difficult in practice: In multi-task RL, state of the art methods often fail to outperform a degenerate solution that simply learns each task separately.

arxiv-2306-06717.title: PWR-Align: Leveraging Part-Whole Relationships for Part-wise Rigid Point Cloud Registration in Mixed Reality Applications
arxiv-2306-06717.creator: Manorama Jha, Bhaskar Banerjee
arxiv-2306-06717.description: Abstract We present an efficient and robust point cloud registration (PCR) workflow for part-wise rigid point cloud alignment using the Microsoft HoloLens 2. Point Cloud Registration (PCR) is an important problem in Augmented and Mixed Reality use cases, and we present a study for a special class of non-rigid transformations.

arxiv-2401-09745.title: Impact of Limited Statistics on the Measured Hyper-Order Cumulants of Net-Proton Distributions in Heavy-Ion Collisions
arxiv-2401-09745.creator: Lizhu Chen, Ye-Yin Zhao, Yunshan Cheng, Gang Wang, Zhiming Li, Yuanfang Wu
arxiv-2401-09745.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lizhu Chen, Ye-Yin Zhao, Yunshan Cheng, Gang Wang, Zhiming Li, Yuanfang Wu. Hyper-order cumulants C 5 / C 1 C_{5}/C_{1} and C 6 / C 2 C_{6}/C_{2} of net-baryon distributions are anticipated to offer crucial insights into the phase transition from quark-gluon plasma to hadronic matter in heavy-ion collisions. However, the accuracy of C 5 C_{5} and C 6 C_{6} is highly contingent on the fine shape of the distribution’s tail, the detectable range of which could be essentially truncated by low statistics.

arxiv-2404-16656.title: A Self-Organizing Clustering System for Unsupervised Distribution Shift Detection
arxiv-2404-16656.creator: Sebastián Basterrech, Line Clemmensen, Gerardo Rubino
arxiv-2404-16656.description: Abstract Modeling non-stationary data is a challenging problem in the field of continual learning, and data distribution shifts may result in negative consequences on the performance of a machine learning model. Classic learning tools are often vulnerable to perturbations of the input covariates, and are sensitive to outliers and noise, and some tools are based on rigid algebraic assumptions.

arxiv-2411-09122.title: Complex Bott Periodicity in algebraic geometry
arxiv-2411-09122.creator: Hannah Larson and Ravi Vakil appendix by Benjamin Church
arxiv-2411-09122.description: Abstract . We state and prove a form of Bott periodicity (for U ⁡ ( n ) U(n) ) in an algebraic setting (so, G ​ L ​ ( n ) GL(n) ) which makes sense over Z \mathbb{Z} , which also specializes to Bott periodicity in the usual sense (hence giving yet another proof of classical Bott periodicity).

arxiv-2502-09251.title: Recipe : Hardware-Accelerated Replication Protocols 110
arxiv-2502-09251.creator: Dimitra Giantsidi, Emmanouil Giortamis, Julian Pritzi, Maurice Bailleu, Manos Kapritsos, Pramod Bhatotia
arxiv-2502-09251.description: Abstract . Replication protocols are fundamental to distributed systems, ensuring consistency, reliability, and fault tolerance. Traditional Crash Fault Tolerant (CFT) replication protocols assume a fail-stop model, making them unsuitable for untrusted cloud environments where adversaries (e.g., co-located tenants or a malicious administrator) or software bugs may lead to Byzantine behavior.

arxiv-2506-05105.title: Classification and enumeration of solid-solid phase transition mechanisms
arxiv-2506-05105.creator: Fang-Cheng Wang, Qi-Jun Ye, Yu-Cheng Zhu, Xin-Zheng Li
arxiv-2506-05105.description: Abstract Crystal-structure match (CSM), the atom-to-atom correspondence between two crystalline phases, is used extensively to describe solid-solid phase transition (SSPT) mechanisms. However, existing computational methods cannot account for all possible CSMs. Here, we propose a formalism to classify all CSMs into a tree structure, which is independent of the choices of unit cell and supercell.

arxiv-2507-05005.title: Approximation of the Lévy-driven stochastic heat equation on the sphere Thanks: Acknowledgment: This research was funded in parts by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) [10.55776/DOC78], by the European Union (ERC, StochMan, 101088589), by the Swedish Research Council (VR) through grant no. 2020-04170,
arxiv-2507-05005.creator: Annika Lang, Andrea Papini, Verena Schwarz
arxiv-2507-05005.description: Abstract . The stochastic heat equation on the sphere driven by additive Lévy random field is approximated by a spectral method in space and forward and backward Euler–Maruyama schemes in time, in analogy to the Wiener case. New regularity results are proven for the stochastic heat equation.

arxiv-2510-05144.title: SynCED-EnDe 2025: A Synthetic and Curated English - German Dataset for Critical Error Detection in Machine Translation
arxiv-2510-05144.creator: Muskaan ChopraRheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Bonn, GermanyLamarr Institute for Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence, Germany chopra.muskaan@uni-bonn.de, Lorenz SparrenbergRheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Bonn, GermanyLamarr Institute for Machine Learning and Artificial In
arxiv-2510-05144.description: Abstract Critical Error Detection (CED) in machine translation aims to determine whether a translation is safe to use or contains unacceptable deviations in meaning. While the WMT21 English-German CED dataset provided the first benchmark, it is limited in scale, label balance, domain coverage, and temporal freshness.

arxiv-2511-11922.title: Additive Large Language Models for Semi-Structured Text
arxiv-2511-11922.creator: Karthikeyan K, Raghuveer Thirukovalluru, David Carlson
arxiv-2511-11922.description: Abstract Large Language Models have advanced clinical text classification, but their opaque predictions remain a critical barrier to practical adoption in research and clinical settings where investigators and physicians need to understand which parts of a patient’s record drive risk signals.

arxiv-2511-14473.title: Learning Subglacial Bed Topography from Sparse Radar with Physics-Guided Residuals
arxiv-2511-14473.creator: Bayu Adhi Tama, Jianwu Wang, Vandana Janeja, Mostafa Cham
arxiv-2511-14473.description: Abstract Accurate subglacial bed topography is essential for ice-sheet modeling, yet radar observations are sparse and uneven. We propose a physics-guided residual learning framework that predicts bed thickness residuals over a BedMachine prior and reconstructs bed from the observed surface. A DeepLabV3 + + decoder over a standard encoder (e.g.

arxiv-2601-13106.title: Product-State Approximation Algorithms for the Transverse Field Ising Model
arxiv-2601-13106.creator: Vincenzo Lipardi, David Mestel, Georgios Stamoulis
arxiv-2601-13106.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Vincenzo Lipardi, David Mestel, Georgios Stamoulis. We study classical polynomial-time approximation algorithms for the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) Hamiltonian, allowing a mixture of ferromagnetic and anti-ferromagnetic interactions between pairs of qbits, alongside transverse field terms with arbitrary non-negative weights.

arxiv-2605-25820.creator: Yulin Yuan Zhejiang University yulinyuan@zju.edu.cn Hongshuo Zhao ZJUI-UIUC Institute hongshuo.24@intl.zju.edu.cn Xiangming Meng ZJUI-UIUC Institute xiangmingmeng@intl.zju.edu.cn

pmc-10548645.title: Community-based organizations’ perspectives on piloting health and social care integration in North Carolina
pmc-10548645.creator: Raman Nohria, Junette Yu, Karissa Tu, Grace Feng, Shemecka Mcneil, Fred Johnson, Michelle Lyn, Karen Scherr
pmc-10548645.description: BackgroundCommunity-based organizations (CBOs) are key players in health and social care integration initiatives, yet little is known about CBO perspectives and experiences in these pilot programs. Understanding CBO perspectives is vital to identifying best practices for successful medical and social care integration.

pmc-10636890.title: Regulatory enforcement of the marketing of fixed-dose combinations in India: a case study of systemic antibiotics
pmc-10636890.creator: Petra Brhlikova, Aashna Mehta, Patricia McGettigan, Allyson M Pollock, Peter Roderick, Habib Hasan Farooqui
pmc-10636890.description: BackgroundIn India, states have licensed the manufacture of large numbers of fixed-dose combination (FDC) drugs without the required prior approval of the central regulator. This paper describes two major regulatory initiatives to address the problem, which began in 2007 and 2013, and examines whether they have been sufficient to remove centrally unapproved systemic antibiotic FDCs from the market.

pmc-10740108.title: Comparison of the methylglyoxal scavenging effects of kaempferol and glutathione and the consequences for the toxicity of methylglyoxal in SH-SY5Y cells
pmc-10740108.creator: Liang Zheng, Wouter Bakker, Ignacio Miro Estruch, Frances Widjaja, Ivonne M.C.M. Rietjens
pmc-10740108.description: Graphical abstract Introduction Methylglyoxal (MGO) is a highly reactive α-dicarbonyl compound formed endogenous but also widely distributed in various foods and beverages such as roasted meat, cookies, bread, honey, coffee, milk, and beer (Degen et al., 2012, Maasen et al., 2021).

pmc-11368419.title: Cautionary tales on the use of proxies to estimate body size and form of extinct animals
pmc-11368419.creator: Joel H. Gayford, Russell K. Engelman, Phillip C. Sternes, Wayne M. Itano, Mohamad Bazzi, Alberto Collareta, Rodolfo Salas‐Gismondi, Kenshu Shimada
pmc-11368419.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Body size is of fundamental importance to our understanding of extinct organisms. Physiology, ecology and life history are all strongly influenced by body size and shape, which ultimately determine how a species interacts with its environment. Reconstruction of body size and form in extinct animals provides insight into the dynamics underlying community composition and faunal turnover in past ecosystems and broad macroevolutionary trends.

pmc-11440089.title: DeepPBI-KG: a deep learning method for the prediction of phage-bacteria interactions based on key genes
pmc-11440089.creator: Tongqing Wei, Chenqi Lu, Hanxiao Du, Qianru Yang, Xin Qi, Yankun Liu, Yi Zhang, Chen Chen, Yutong Li, Yuanhao Tang, Wen-Hong Zhang, Xu Tao, Ning Jiang
pmc-11440089.description: Phages, the natural predators of bacteria, were discovered more than 100 years ago. However, increasing antimicrobial resistance rates have revitalized phage research. Methods that are more time-consuming and efficient than wet-laboratory experiments are needed to help screen phages quickly for therapeutic use. Traditional computational methods usually ignore the fact that phage-bacteria interactions are achieved by key genes and proteins.

pmc-11452301.title: AMP‐dependent kinase stimulates the expression of αKlotho
pmc-11452301.creator: Julia Vogt, Lisa Wolf, Ludwig E Hoelzle, Martina Feger, Michael Föller
pmc-11452301.description: Renal αKlotho along with fibroblast growth factor 23 regulates phosphate and vitamin D metabolism. Its cleavage yields soluble Klotho controlling intracellular processes. αKlotho has anti‐inflammatory and antioxidant effects and is nephro‐ and cardioprotective. AMP‐dependent kinase (AMPK) is a nephro‐ and cardioprotective energy sensor.

pmc-11483398.title: Design, Synthesis, and Characterization of HBP-Vectorized Methotrexate Prodrug Molecule 1102–39: Evaluation of In Vitro Cytotoxicity Activity in Cell Culture Models, Preliminary In Vivo Safety and Efficacy Results in Rodents
pmc-11483398.creator: Maxim Egorov, Jean-Yves Goujon, Marie Sicard, Christelle Moal, Samuel Pairel, Ronan Le Bot
pmc-11483398.description: A novel bone-targeted prodrug, 1102–39, is discussed with the aim of enhancing the therapeutic effects of methotrexate (MTX) within bone tissues while minimizing systemic toxicity. Within the 1102–39 molecule, the central linker part forms a cleavable ester group, with MTX being also linked by a stable imine bond to the specially designed hydroxybisphosphonic (HBP) vector.

pmc-11534214.title: Correlations between nutritional indicators and cognitive function in patients with stable schizophrenia in a hospital setting
pmc-11534214.creator: Binyou Wang, Yong Zhou, Han Yu, Techeng Jiang, Kezhi Liu, Jianlin Pu, Yilin Wang
pmc-11534214.description: Background and objectivesCognitive impairment is a core feature of schizophrenia, and it is now clear that there is a link between nutritional indicators and cognitive functioning. This study aimed to investigate correlations between three nutritional indicators (prognostic nutritional index [PNI], geriatric nutritional risk index [GNRI], and controlling nutritional status score [CONUT]) and cognitive function in hospitalized patients with stable schizophrenia.

pmc-11786002.title: Assessment of the pterygoid hamulus dimensions and morphology in Iranian women using cone-beam computed tomography
pmc-11786002.creator: Zahra Mahdavi, Ladan Hafezi
pmc-11786002.description: Background. Understanding the characteristics of the pterygoid hamulus (PH) is crucial for diagnosing and treating various oropharyngeal and craniofacial conditions. It also aids in interpreting radiographs and diagnosing unexplained oropharyngeal pains. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is a valuable tool, offering clinical insights into this previously understudied area.

pmc-11859164.title: Gestational age and sex interaction and risk for autism spectrum disorder in extremely preterm newborns: an 18‑month follow‑up study
pmc-11859164.creator: L. Pina-Camacho, J. Merchan-Naranjo, E. Rodriguez-Toscano, L. Martin, C. Romero, L. Boada, S. Zeballos, M. Arriaga, D. Blanco-Bravo
pmc-11859164.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionExtremely preterm newborns - EPTN (born ≤28 weeks gestational age) are at increased risk of developing autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Demographic and perinatal risk factors associated with ASD risk in EPTN are understudied.Objectives(i) In EPTN and born at full-term healthy controls (HC), to characterize the emergence of ASD traits and autistic symptom load at age 18 months; (ii) in EPTN, to identify the influence of perinatal characteristics such as sex and gestational age on autistic symptom load at corrected-age 18 months.MethodsObservational, longitudinal,

pmc-12643074.title: Breaking the Stalemate: How Italy’s Non-Medical Health Professions Are Trapped by Redundant Roles and Ineffective Degrees
pmc-12643074.creator: ROBERTO TEDESCHI
pmc-12643074.description: pediatric nurse, midwife, physiotherapist, speech therapist, podiatrist, therapist in neuro and psychomotor therapy of developmental age, psychiatric rehabilitation technician, occupational therapist, professional educator, medical radiology technician, biomedical laboratory technician, orthopedic technician, audiometry technician, hearing aid technician, dental hygienist, dietitian, neurophysiopathology technician, cardiovascular and perfusion technician, and, most recently, osteopath [1].

pmc-12735050.title: Prevalence of Cardiovascular–Kidney–Metabolic (CKM) Syndrome in Lithuanian Adults: Insights from a Nationwide Real-World Study Using Electronic Health Records
pmc-12735050.creator: Gediminas Urbonas, Indrė Čeponienė, Inga Arūnė Bumblytė, Marius Miglinas, Lina Gatelytė, Živilė Steponkutė, Aušra Degutytė, Ingrida Grabauskytė, Džilda Veličkienė
pmc-12735050.description: Background and Objectives: Cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome reflects the interconnection between metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and cardiovascular disease (CVD). Despite increasing awareness, population-based data on CKM syndrome are limited, particularly in Europe. This study assessed the prevalence of CKM syndrome and the use of renal and cardiac biomarkers in Lithuania.

pmc-13084638.title: AI Use for Medical Students: Impact on Clinical Skill Acquisition and Retention. A Systematic Review
pmc-13084638.creator: Jonathan Turney, Tim M Young, Dhyana R Chauhan, Roshni Beeharry, Mohammad Mahmud
pmc-13084638.description: PurposeArtificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in undergraduate medical education but has a potentially negative impact on clinical reasoning development. Specifically, the use of AI in medical student education may lead to deskilling and upskilling inhibition - where automation reduces practice or limits skill development - potentially impairing clinical reasoning.

pmc-13198522.title: Sleep quality after shoulder arthroplasty – A systematic review
pmc-13198522.creator: Kalter Hali, Marc A Manzo, Sean Mckellar, Matthew J Raleigh, Ujash Sheth
pmc-13198522.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundShoulder arthroplasty has been shown to improve pain and function. However, its effect on postoperative sleep quality remains poorly defined. The purpose of this systematic review is to summarize changes in sleep quality after shoulder arthroplasty.MethodsMEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 31 October 2025, for studies reporting postoperative sleep outcomes following primary shoulder arthroplasty with at least one reported postoperative sleep-related outcome.

pmc-13247332.title: Integrative analysis of cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers, metabolomics, and polygenic risk reveals novel metabolite associations with Alzheimer's disease
pmc-13247332.creator: Marcelo Francia, Naren Ramesh, Toni Boltz, Merel Bot, Wiesje M van der Flier, Pieter Jelle Visser, Sven van der Lee, Charlotte E Teunissen, Yolande AL Pijnenburg, Anouk den Braber, Loes Olde Loohuis, Lianne M Reus, Betty M Tijms, Roel A Ophoff
pmc-13247332.description: BackgroundCerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metabolomics offers an opportunity to investigate in vivo biological pathways impacted in the human brain by Alzheimer's disease (AD). While impairments in brain glucose metabolism and lipid homeostasis are implicated in AD, the underlying metabolic pathways remain unclear. Genotype information can also be leveraged to study associations between CSF metabolites and AD genetic risk.

pmc-13372797.title: Clarification on the Measurement of Vertebral Body Loss in the Spinal Tuberculosis Instability Score
pmc-13372797.creator: Abhishek Dussa
pmc-13372797.description: provides an objective framework for assessing surgical candidacy and represents a valuable contribution to the management of this challenging condition. 1 One of the principal variables in the scoring system is the vertebral body loss (VBL)-segmental ratio, calculated as previously described by the authors.

pmc-13455148.title: Multimodal opioid-free anesthesia containing esketamine versus opioid-based anesthesia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13455148.creator: Ye Fang, Meiling Gao, Xin Wang, Bin Zheng, Meiling He, Xingxing Zeng, Yu Shi, Linan Li, Boyu Zhang, Yang Xu, Xingrui Gong
pmc-13455148.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe paradigm shift toward opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) is gaining traction, yet evidence regarding specific viable alternatives remains fragmented. This meta-analysis comprehensively evaluates the efficacy and safety of multimodal OFA regimens containing esketamine compared to traditional opioid-based anesthesia (OBA).MethodsThis study conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis by searching the electronic databases PubMed, The Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase, including randomized controlled trials published from inception to September 20, 2024.

pmc-13692741.title: Atomic-Scale Anisotropy Competition Drives Spin Reorientation in Intercalated 2D Ferromagnets
pmc-13692741.creator: Yu-Sheng Tseng, Wan-Sheng Tang, Bao-Huei Huang, Yu-Hui Tang
pmc-13692741.description: Precise control over magnetic anisotropy (MA) in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals ferromagnets is essential for advancing next-generation spintronics; however, the atomic-scale mechanisms dictating intercalation-induced MA modulation remain largely unresolved. In this study, we elucidate the microscopic origins of the complex magnetic phase diagram in Cr-intercalated CrTe2 by integrating layer-resolved density functional theory-based spin–orbit torque (DFT-SOT) calculations with micromagnetic simulations.
